claims.text:
gan-forger-detective

**Identity / target / source:** `ai:gan-forger-detective` → `ai-gan-forger-detective` → `src/demos/ai/ai-gan-forger-detective`; source `company/domains/proposals/2026-10-18-ai-map-expansion.json#concepts/78`; brief `company/domains/briefs/2026-10-19-ai-next30e.md#1-gan-forger-detective`. **Packet:** G1. **Level / prerequisites:** core; `ai:decision-boundary`.

**Nearest / distinct payoff:** decision-boundary classifies fixed points; here a discriminator update changes the signal for a separate generator probability.

**Computed primary model:** Two outcomes A/B, real p=[.5,.5], generator q=[.8,.2] parameterized qA=sigmoid(theta), theta=ln4. Discriminator logits d=[0,0], D=sigmoid(d). Discriminator loss −sum p_i ln D_i −sum q_i ln(1−D_i); gradient_i=(p_i+q_i)D_i−p_i=[.15,−.15]. Eta1 gives d=[−.15,.15], D≈[.46257,.53743]. Then freeze D; non-saturating generator loss −qA ln DA−(1−qA)ln DB has theta-gradient qA(1−qA)(ln DB−ln DA)=.024. Eta1 gives theta=ln4−.024, reducing qA toward.5.

**Countercase / boundary:** If the discriminator stays constantD=[.5,.5], generator gradient0 despite wrong q. The discriminator consumes real and generated distributions; only this generator update consumes its scalar losses. Do not claim GAN generators can never access training examples, or that alternating updates always converge.

**Prediction / transfer recall:** Predict the direction of qA after D has learned; recall reversing real p to[.9,.1] at the same original q makes the first discriminator signal favour A instead.

**Intervention / retained witness:** Train discriminator then Train generator recompute separate logits/probabilities/loss signals. Constant detector control restarts with frozen.5/.5 and exposes zero signal, retaining the original changed-generator witness. Candidate outcomes, not borrowed pictures.

**Source obligation:** [Goodfellow et al. original PDF](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1406.2661), opened2026-10-19, §3 Eq1, non-saturating generator alternative and Algorithm1 (PDFpp3–4), §4.1 optimal discriminator. These explicit finite gradients/limited classifiers are local derivations, not the paper’s image experiments or a convergence claim.
